worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=50,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=\frac{432}{900}=0.48.$

Now, since

$$
np=50(0.48)=24>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=50(1-0.48)=26>5,
$$

and the $n=50$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.48,\frac{0.48(1-0.48)}{50}) \\  & ∼N(0.48,0.0050).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the probability we wish to find. If between $20$ and $23$ of students in the sample are male, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{50}\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le \frac{23}{50} \\ 0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p} & \le 0.46.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the probability we wish to find is
$P(0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.46).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.4\le \overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.46) & =P(\frac{0.4-0.48}{\sqrt{0.0050}}\le Z\le \frac{0.46-0.48}{\sqrt{0.0050}}) \\  & ≈P(-1.13\le Z\le -0.28) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.28)-P(Z\le -1.13) \\  & =Φ(-0.28)-Φ(-1.13)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.28)=0.3897,\,Φ(-1.13)=0.1292.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.4<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.46) & =Φ(-0.28)-Φ(-1.13) \\  & =0.3897-0.1292 \\  & =0.2605.\end{aligned}
$$
